3.speaker: Narrator
3.text: I had been invited to Cavette, the capital of Morella, for a meeting with Prime Minister Alma Saltana.

5.speaker: Player_Romus
5.text: "It's good to see you again, Madam Prime Minister."

6.speaker: Player_Romus
6.text: "Quite a lovely park you have here."

7.speaker: Player_Romus
7.text: "I don't have all day. Let's get down to it, shall we?"

9.speaker: Narrator
9.text: She smiled and motioned for me to follow her.

12.speaker: Alma Saltana
12.text: "The Moridian emperors found beauty in control. Today, we find it in freedom."

13.speaker: Alma Saltana
13.text: "We didn't part under the best of circumstances last time."

14.speaker: Alma Saltana
14.text: "But everyone deserves a second chance. That's my philosophy, at least."

15.speaker: Narrator
15.text: She motioned for me to follow her.

16.speaker: Narrator
16.text: A barely marked path led into a dense bamboo grove. We walked in, shadowed by our guards.

17.speaker: Alma Saltana
17.text: "This was all planted after the Valgs left. Amazing how fast it grows."

18.speaker: Narrator
18.text: On it was a square-jawed man -- Axel Reinhart's exact double -- triumphantly hoisting his sword atop the park's central hill.

19.speaker: Narrator
19.text: An inscription below it read: "In Commemoration of the Brave Deeds of Otto Reinhart, Viceroy of Pales and Loyal Servant of the Valgos Empire."

20.speaker: Player_Romus
20.text: "I'm surprised you haven't gotten rid of this. Why keep around reminders of the Valgos occupation?"

21.speaker: Player_Romus
21.text: "The Valgos Empire used our family's conflict as an excuse for a land grab. Both of our countries lost territory."

22.speaker: Narrator
22.text: At the end of the path, we came to a small cylindrical building that looked strikingly different from anything else in the park.

23.speaker: Alma Saltana
23.text: "A traditional Morellan teahouse. Historically, a place for exchange and a refuge from prying eyes."

24.speaker: Narrator
24.text: We had a seat inside as our guards kept watch outdoors.

25.speaker: Narrator
25.text: The low-ceilinged room was decorated wall-to-wall in colorful woven fabrics. In its center, smoke rose from a roaring fire pit up through a hole in the middle of the ceiling.

26.speaker: Narrator
26.text: A waiter came by with a tray of sukhar, Morellan tea biscuits.

27.speaker: Player_Romus
27.text: "Why, thank you. I'd love a biscuit."

28.speaker: Player_Romus
28.text: "They look delicious, but I ate before I came here."

29.speaker: Alma Saltana
29.text: "This is Morellan tea culture, {RiziaDLCText.SaltanaToPlayer}. It's impolite to refuse an offer of food."

30.speaker: Player_Romus
30.text: "All right. In that case, just one."

31.speaker: Narrator
31.text: The waiter placed a pair of intricately ornamented tea glasses in front of us and filled them up.

32.speaker: Narrator
32.text: We each took a biscuit off the tray.

33.speaker: Narrator
33.text: The waiter, however, seemed to have disappeared without serving us anything to drink.

34.speaker: Alma Saltana
34.text: "Hmm, that's an oversight. Well, I'm sure he'll be over with our tea shortly."

35.speaker: Narrator
35.text: I noticed Saltana had left her biscuit uneaten.

37.speaker: Alma Saltana
37.text: "I admit that before the nationalization vote, I had held out hope that your kingdom would recognize its debt to Morella and agree to our plan."

38.speaker: Alma Saltana
38.text: "I was disappointed when that turned out not to be the case."

39.speaker: Narrator
39.text: As we kept walking, I noticed the corner of a wooden object peeking out from behind the stalks.

42.speaker: Narrator
42.text: It appeared to be a memorial plaque, carved in traditional Valgish style.

43.speaker: Alma Saltana
43.text: "Like it or not, it was part of our history."

44.speaker: Player_Romus
44.text: "Morella went up against House Toras. What did you think would happen?"

45.speaker: Alma Saltana
45.text: "The taking of Cavette. Our punishment for siding with the wrong house in your War of Succession."

46.speaker: Player_Romus
46.text: "What a tragedy. Our houses should've found a peaceful compromise instead of dragging other countries into battle."

47.speaker: Alma Saltana
47.text: "It was the Empire of Moridia that got involved. If I had been in charge back then, I would have had the good sense to stay out of it entirely."

48.speaker: Alma Saltana
48.text: "We lost one of our most important cities and our access to the Antacean. There is no comparison."

49.speaker: Alma Saltana
49.text: "I agree, with the caveat that Moridia wasn't dragged. They saw their alliance with the Azaro family as a way to gain power over Rizia."

50.speaker: Alma Saltana
50.text: "Losing territory to Valgsland was fair enough punishment."

51.speaker: Alma Saltana
51.text: "At least we were able to take back the territory we lost."

53.speaker: Alma Saltana
53.text: "Thankfully, we were able to get it all back after the revolution."

54.speaker: Alma Saltana
54.text: "Just as the Republic of Valgsland is part of our present."

55.speaker: Player_Romus
55.text: "My hands were tied by Rizian business and governmental interests, Madam Prime Minister. Surely you understand."

56.speaker: Player_Romus
56.text: "I really must decline. I'm positively stuffed."

58.speaker: Alma Saltana
58.text: "Very well. I hope you at least have room for tea."

59.speaker: Narrator
59.text: The waiter placed a pair of intricately ornamented tea glasses in front of us and filled them up.

63.speaker: Player_Romus
63.text: "I am all for increasing Morella's profit share. But nationalization was simply too extreme of a solution."

64.speaker: Narrator
64.text: The biscuit had drained all the moisture from my mouth, rendering my speech incoherent.

65.speaker: Player_Romus
65.text: "Lespia and Rizia stand firm in our demand that the MITZ stay as it is. No new proposal will get by us."

66.speaker: Player_Romus
66.text: "Sorry, but the Rizian economic situation is such that I could not risk a potential loss of gold revenue."

67.speaker: Alma Saltana
67.text: "I would like to once again emphasize that the country of Morella will not go back to the way things were."

68.speaker: Narrator
68.text: My tongue felt like it was covered in sawdust. I tried in vain to swallow.

69.speaker: Player_Romus
69.text: "You're shit out of luck, lady. Rizia isn't budging either."

70.speaker: Player_Romus
70.text: "Rizia is perfectly willing to meet any demands you might have. We all want the same thing here."

71.speaker: Player_Romus
71.text: "Where is that waiter with our tea?"

73.speaker: Player_Romus
73.text: "It's disgusting how the Reinhart family has managed to stay in power all these years."

74.speaker: Player_Romus
74.text: "How did you manage to reclaim such a large swathe of land, anyway?"

75.speaker: Player_Romus
75.text: "I'm surprised that Morella doesn't still bear a grudge against the Valgs."

76.speaker: Player_Romus
76.text: "Valgsland may be a republic now, but its motivations haven't changed. You should be wary of your new friend Mr. Hegel."

77.speaker: Alma Saltana
77.text: "Their current administration has made an admirable attempt to atone for the Valgos Empire's misdeeds."

79.speaker: Alma Saltana
79.text: "I hate to admit it, but my right-wing predecessors happened to be very good strategists."

80.speaker: Alma Saltana
80.text: "Which doesn't mean I trust Chancellor Hegel without reservations, of course."

81.speaker: Alma Saltana
81.text: "His administration has made an admirable attempt to atone for the Valgos Empire's misdeeds."

85.speaker: Alma Saltana
85.text: "The world would be a better place if more countries followed its example."

89.speaker: Alma Saltana
89.text: "Which doesn't mean I trust him without reservations, of course."

90.speaker: Alma Saltana
90.text: "The world would be a better place if more countries followed his example."

93.speaker: Player_Romus
93.text: "That's different. My family was chosen by God to rule."

97.speaker: Player_Romus
97.text: "Yes, exactly. Power should be determined by the people's will, not by blood."

102.speaker: Player_Romus
102.text: "Do not question the legitimacy of my family's reign, Madam Prime Minister."

103.speaker: Player_Romus
103.text: "Not the same. Pales never rightfully belonged to the Reinharts to begin with."

104.speaker: Alma Saltana
104.text: "An odd thing for a monarch to say. But I agree."

105.speaker: Narrator
105.text: She disguised a laugh as a cough.

111.speaker: Alma Saltana
111.text: "Believe me, there is no love lost between Morella and the Reinharts. But we're happy to let them keep their little piece of land. As long as they stay there."

117.speaker: Player_Romus
117.text: "And the Reinharts? What do you think of them?"

118.speaker: Alma Saltana
118.text: "It helped that with its coast blocked, Morella was compelled to invest more into its air force."

119.speaker: Alma Saltana
119.text: "When Lespia started sending Pales planes, we had our own ready to counter them."

120.speaker: Alma Saltana
120.text: "Cavette and the coast were relatively new additions to the Grand Duchy."

121.speaker: Alma Saltana
121.text: "There were still plenty of Morellans living there, ready to rise up and take their land back."

122.speaker: Player_Romus
122.text: "Impressive. I'd love to learn more about those planes."

123.speaker: Player_Romus
123.text: "Did you ever feel tempted to take over *all* of Pales?"

124.speaker: Alma Saltana
124.text: "Even if we had the might to do so, we couldn't have done it without making enemies of Rizia. Or am I wrong?"

125.speaker: Narrator
125.text: We drank. The tea was delicious.

127.speaker: Alma Saltana
127.text: "Neither of us want to resort to military measures. But I will say this."

128.speaker: Alma Saltana
128.text: "Both Valgsland and Morella have kept a close eye on the Rizian populace. Particularly your youth."

129.speaker: Alma Saltana
129.text: "I believe there's a certain... spirit in your country. One that, if given the proper support and channels, could bring about monumental change."

130.speaker: Player_Romus
130.text: "You're keeping an eye on our youth? That's disturbing."

131.speaker: Player_Romus
131.text: "Is that a threat, Ms. Saltana? You'll spark a revolution in Rizia if you don't get what you want?"

132.speaker: Player_Romus
132.text: "I don't care. Just bring me some tea, dammit!"

134.speaker: Alma Saltana
134.text: "If you're willing to agree on an ITZ proposal that is fair and equitable towards Morella, you won't have to find out whether I'm right."

135.speaker: Narrator
135.text: She gave a tiny nod. Our waiter stepped over with a pot of tea and two intricately ornamented ceramic cups.

136.speaker: Narrator
136.text: Once he'd filled mine, I drank immediately. The hot tea nearly scalded my throat, but I could speak again.

138.speaker: Player_Romus
138.text: "I've been willing to negotiate with you from the start, Ms. Saltana. No need for the biscuit torture."

139.speaker: Player_Romus
139.text: "Phew. That biscuit was drier than the last AN session."

140.speaker: Player_Romus
140.text: "If that was an attempt to intimidate me, you have failed."

141.speaker: Alma Saltana
141.text: "I am truly sorry. I have no idea what took our waiter so long."

143.speaker: Alma Saltana
143.text: "I admit that before the nationalization vote, I had held out hope that your kingdom would recognize its debt to Morella and agree to our plan."

144.speaker: Alma Saltana
144.text: "I was disappointed when that turned out not to be the case."

145.speaker: Player_Romus
145.text: "My hands were tied, Madam Prime Minister. Surely you understand."

146.speaker: Player_Romus
146.text: "I am all for increasing Morella's profit share. But nationalization was simply too extreme of a solution."

147.speaker: Player_Romus
147.text: "Lespia and Rizia stand firm in our convictions. Morella does not have the right to take our profits away from us."

148.speaker: Player_Romus
148.text: "Sorry, but the Rizian economy is dependent on gold from the MITZ. We can offer you other things, but the Trade Zone conditions must stay the same."

149.speaker: Alma Saltana
149.text: "We don't wish to antagonize either Rizia or Lespia. But we will not go back to the way things were."

150.speaker: Player_Romus
150.text: "You're out of luck, then. Rizia isn't going to budge."

151.speaker: Player_Romus
151.text: "Nor will we. Even with nationalization off the table, we are committed to improving the situation in the MITZ."

152.speaker: Player_Romus
152.text: "And *we* will not let Valgsland and the CSP get their grubby hands into our business."

155.speaker: Alma Saltana
155.text: "Neither of us want to resort to military measures. But I will say this."

156.speaker: Alma Saltana
156.text: "Both Valgsland and Morella have kept a close eye on the Rizian populace. Particularly your youth."

158.speaker: Player_Romus
158.text: "Is that a threat, Ms. Saltana? You'll spark a revolution in Rizia if you don't get what you want?"

159.speaker: Alma Saltana
159.text: "I believe there's a certain... spirit in your country. One that, if given the proper support and channels, could bring about monumental change."

160.speaker: Player_Romus
160.text: "You're keeping an eye on our youth? That's disturbing."

161.speaker: Player_Romus
161.text: "I get the point. I'm willing to negotiate with you."

165.speaker: Player_Romus
165.text: "You made your point. Can we discuss the agreement now?"

168.speaker: Alma Saltana
168.text: "It's good to know that you're flexible."

175.speaker: Alma Saltana
175.text: "I don't need to tell you how grateful I am for your kingdom's vote."

176.speaker: Player_Romus
176.text: "For the well-being of your workers and the good of your country, there was no other way I could have voted."

177.speaker: Player_Romus
177.text: "Don't get me wrong, Ms. Saltana. I will not walk away with nothing."

178.speaker: Player_Romus
178.text: "It was a sacrifice. But I was willing to make it to get Lespia and its Arcasian puppetmasters out of the MITZ."

179.speaker: Player_Romus
179.text: "Not so fast. Nationalization won't happen unless we come away with a final proposal that Rizia is happy with."

181.speaker: Alma Saltana
181.text: "If that was the reason for your vote, I may have to disappoint you."

183.speaker: Alma Saltana
183.text: "I'm very glad you see it that way."

187.speaker: Alma Saltana
187.text: "That's surprising to hear, coming from you. But welcome."

188.speaker: Alma Saltana
188.text: "Of course, I want the final agreement to be favorable for all four parties involved."

190.speaker: Alma Saltana
190.text: "And I am keeping an open mind as we discuss the proposal today."

191.speaker: Alma Saltana
191.text: "I want the final agreement to be favorable for all four parties involved."

192.speaker: Player_Romus
192.text: "You might as well give up trying to court Lespia's favor. Alvarez isn't willing to budge."

193.speaker: Alma Saltana
193.text: "Obviously, I want the final agreement to be favorable for all four parties involved."

194.speaker: Player_Romus
194.text: "That's the spirit. Valgsland, Rizia and Lespia all deserve to be compensated."

195.speaker: Player_Romus
195.text: "I have a vague hunch that you won't be able to please Valgsland and Lespia at the same time."

196.speaker: Player_Romus
196.text: "It doesn't matter whether everyone likes it. What matters is whether Morella gets the justice it deserves."

197.speaker: Alma Saltana
197.text: "I want the final agreement to be favorable for all four parties involved. Lespia included."

198.speaker: Player_Romus
198.text: "So do I. But earning my kingdom's favor will not be simple."

199.speaker: Alma Saltana
199.text: "The investments that you've made in the MITZ will be recognized."

202.speaker: Alma Saltana
202.text: "I am not trying to court Lespia's favor. But I don't want to shut them out of this proposal, either."

203.speaker: Player_Romus
203.text: "Well, I will not be satisfied with any agreement in which Lespia gets more than Rizia."

204.speaker: Alma Saltana
204.text: "Thank you for that. But I do want to acknowledge the investments your countries have made."

206.speaker: Alma Saltana
206.text: "We haven't even properly started our discussion yet."

207.speaker: Alma Saltana
207.text: "It's certainly not my intention to grant one country a better deal than another."

208.speaker: Alma Saltana
208.text: "As I said during the board meeting, my proposal involves the purchase of Rizia, Lespia and Valgsland's ITZ assets by a newly formed subsidiary of Morella's state-owned mining company."

209.speaker: Alma Saltana
209.text: "Each country would have the option of using the money from that sale to buy up to a 20 percent stake in that company."

211.speaker: Narrator
211.text: She tapped her fingers on her teacup.

212.speaker: Player_Romus
212.text: "So in the end, we'd only be losing five percent of our original share. That sounds reasonable."

213.speaker: Player_Romus
213.text: "I'll be honest. Even with a 20 percent share of the MITZ, the regulations you're set on imposing would devastate our economy."

214.speaker: Player_Romus
214.text: "It sounds like you and Chancellor Hegel have given this a lot of thought."

215.speaker: Player_Romus
215.text: "Doesn't selling shares of the MITZ back to us defeat the point of nationalization?"

216.speaker: Alma Saltana
216.text: "The Valgslandian chancellor thought so as well."

217.speaker: Alma Saltana
217.text: "To be honest, he was against the idea of allowing stakeholders to buy back shares."

218.speaker: Alma Saltana
218.text: "That's why I'm prepared to offer additional incentives, material or otherwise."

219.speaker: Alma Saltana
219.text: "I thought so as well. But I'm nonetheless prepared to offer additional incentives, material or otherwise."

220.speaker: Alma Saltana
220.text: "But I convinced him there was a place for both Rizia and Lespia in the MITZ. Just... a smaller one."

221.speaker: Narrator
221.text: She drained her glass and pushed her teacup aside.

222.speaker: Alma Saltana
222.text: "So tell me, {RiziaDLCText.SaltanaToPlayer}. What is it that Rizia wants from Morella?"

224.speaker: Player_Romus
224.text: "Rizia wants to be Morella's sole energy supplier. You will purchase oil or natural gas from us at a price that we determine."

225.speaker: Player_Romus
225.text: "You're aware of our present difficulties with the Zille region. We would ask for your aid in taking it back from Wehlen."

226.speaker: Player_Romus
226.text: "We're involved in an arbitration dispute over the Aureus gas field. We would like your public support in this matter."

227.speaker: Player_Romus
227.text: "I want you to marry me. By bringing back the tradition of intermarriage between your nation and my kingdom, we will reestablish our dominion over South Merkopa."

229.speaker: Alma Saltana
229.text: "You do realize what year it is?"

230.speaker: Narrator
230.text: She seemed to mull it over.

234.speaker: Alma Saltana
234.text: "If Rizia had allowed its revolution to succeed as it should have, you wouldn't be having this problem."

235.speaker: Alma Saltana
235.text: "But all right. What kind of aid would you ask of us?"

239.speaker: Narrator
239.text: She looked me in the eye.

240.speaker: Player_Romus
240.text: "Wehlen's intervention was my father's idea, not mine. My duty is to ensure the peaceful transfer of Zille back to Rizia."

241.speaker: Player_Romus
241.text: "No, we'd be puppets of Arcasia. Which would be a big problem for *you*."

242.speaker: Player_Romus
242.text: "It was not our time. But our revolution may yet arrive."

247.speaker: Player_Romus
247.text: "Are we here to talk politics, or are we making deals? Let's be pragmatic, Ms. Saltana."

249.speaker: Alma Saltana
249.text: "All right. What kind of aid would you ask of us?"

250.speaker: Alma Saltana
250.text: "The king shouldn't be the one to decide when that time comes."

251.speaker: Alma Saltana
251.text: "You don't know that. Perhaps with Morella's assistance, Rizia would have been able to blaze its own trail."

252.speaker: Player_Romus
252.text: "Not every revolution turns out the way you want it to, Ms. Saltana. Can you really say modern-day Derdia is better off than the Empire of Moridia?"

253.speaker: Alma Saltana
253.text: "It would have been, had Arcasia not tried to warp the Moridian revolution to serve its own aims."

254.speaker: Alma Saltana
254.text: "You do seem to be a more enlightened breed of monarch."

260.speaker: Alma Saltana
260.text: "From the looks of it, you seem to be following in your father's repressive footsteps."

261.speaker: Alma Saltana
261.text: "And you're sure that you will have a steady supply of energy to sell us?"

264.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
264.conditionsRaw: (Variable["RiziaDLC.Diplomacy_Lespia_GasField_25PercentDeal"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.Diplomacy_Pales_GasField_Cede"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.Situation_Diplomacy_Pales_ANDORArbitration"] == true) == false

265.speaker: Alma Saltana
265.text: "I won't deny that Morella needs energy."
265.conditionsRaw: (Variable["RiziaDLC.Diplomacy_Lespia_GasField_25PercentDeal"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.Diplomacy_Pales_GasField_Cede"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.Situation_Diplomacy_Pales_ANDORArbitration"] == true) == false

266.speaker: Player_Romus
266.text: "Rizia is providing strategical assistance to certain local factions that support our aims. We'd like Morella's help in covertly shipping supplies to those factions."

267.speaker: Player_Romus
267.text: "Only your diplomatic support. We need as many countries as possible to speak out against Wehlen's decision."

268.speaker: Alma Saltana
268.text: "Ah. So that's your backup plan now that diplomatic efforts have failed."

272.speaker: Alma Saltana
272.text: "Interesting. I thought you were in the midst of diplomatic efforts to recover Zille."

273.speaker: Player_Romus
273.text: "Of course we will. Even a small share of the Aureus gas field will be enough to make us a major energy exporter."

275.speaker: Player_Romus
275.text: "We are. But it can't hurt to have a backup plan."

276.speaker: Player_Romus
276.text: "Our diplomatic efforts won't succeed unless we also have internal pressure coming from within Zille."

277.speaker: Player_Romus
277.text: "You know Wiktor Smolak. Do you really think diplomacy alone will sway him?"

278.speaker: Player_Romus
278.text: "It was always going to come to this. Wiktor Smolak is not a man who can be reasoned with."

279.speaker: Player_Romus
279.text: "Yes, we both tried our best, but were sadly unable to reach an agreement."

280.speaker: Player_Romus
280.text: "'Diplomatic efforts', my foot. Wehlen was trying to extort us."

284.speaker: Alma Saltana
284.text: "Just tell me this. Is the resistance you're supporting violent, or non-violent?"

286.speaker: Alma Saltana
286.text: "I hope today's talk is more successful."

291.speaker: Player_Romus
291.text: "Completely non-violent. Its goal is to increase pro-Rizian sympathies in the region, nothing more."

292.speaker: Player_Romus
292.text: "You're not in a position to ask that. I'm the one making demands of you, remember?"

293.speaker: Player_Romus
293.text: "As this is a confidential operation, I can't share any details with you at this time."

294.speaker: Player_Romus
294.text: "It is a group of freedom fighters trying to cast off the shackles of Wehzek oppression."

297.speaker: Alma Saltana
297.text: "There is a limit to what you can demand, {RiziaDLCText.SaltanaToPlayer}."

300.speaker: Narrator
300.text: She looked unhappy with my answer, but nodded.

305.speaker: Alma Saltana
305.text: "There is nothing I would like more than to condemn Wiktor Smolak and his one-man reign of terror on an international stage."

306.speaker: Alma Saltana
306.text: "But we'd be taking a risk. United Contana is still backing Wehlen through all this."

307.speaker: Player_Romus
307.text: "To hell with United Contana. Partner more closely with Rizia, and you will not need to compromise your values."

308.speaker: Player_Romus
308.text: "You are not in the CSP, Ms. Saltana. You don't need to worry about United Contana's opinion."

309.speaker: Player_Romus
309.text: "Much as I respect Comrade Malenyev, he is in the wrong regarding Wehlen and you know it."

314.speaker: Alma Saltana
314.text: "Partnering with a monarchy *is* a compromise of my values."

315.speaker: Alma Saltana
315.text: "Not *yet*. I don't want to close off that possibility."

317.speaker: Alma Saltana
317.text: "We must be willing to make small compromises for the greater ideological good."

318.speaker: Alma Saltana
318.text: "That won't be enough to protect me should Morella get on the CSP's bad side."

327.speaker: Player_Romus
327.text: "Of course we will. I fully expect that Rizia will win the Aureus gas field arbitration case."

328.speaker: Player_Romus
328.text: "Yes, even if the Aureus gas field arbitration doesn't go our way, we have plenty of alternatives."

329.speaker: Player_Romus
329.text: "That's not for you to worry about."

330.speaker: Player_Romus
330.text: "Yes, we may have lost access to the Aureus field but we have plenty of other energy reserves."

331.speaker: Player_Romus
331.text: "Our oil deal with Wehlen is going through, we'll be able to build a pipeline straight to Morella soon."

332.speaker: Player_Romus
332.text: "Nationalization is also a large commitment, Ms. Saltana."

338.speaker: Player_Romus
338.text: "I was joking. Shame on you for believing I would only see a powerful female leader like you as marriage material."

339.speaker: Player_Romus
339.text: "You asked for Rizia's demands. It was worth a shot."

340.speaker: Player_Romus
340.text: "The year doesn't matter, Ms. Saltana. Marriage is the fastest way to cement a partnership between two countries."

341.speaker: Narrator
341.text: She nearly spat her tea across the table.

342.speaker: Alma Saltana
342.text: "It's completely insulting to treat a female world leader as mere marriage fodder."

343.speaker: Alma Saltana
343.text: "I'm going to have a lot of trouble taking you seriously going forward."

344.speaker: Player_Romus
344.text: "It's not purely for strategic reasons. We could learn to love each other if we tried."

345.speaker: Alma Saltana
345.text: "I forgot this was the way you monarchies function. But no, King Romus, I will not marry you."

347.speaker: Alma Saltana
347.text: "And I'm going to have a lot of trouble taking you seriously going forward."

348.speaker: Alma Saltana
348.text: "You had a strategic marriage with the Rumburgian monarchy for years. So yes, I thought you were serious."

349.speaker: Player_Romus
349.text: "We have covered all of Rizia's demands. Now, which will Morella agree to fulfill?"

350.speaker: Alma Saltana
350.text: "If you can get the Supreme Wiseman to agree to that, we would be interested."

352.speaker: Alma Saltana
352.text: "Please. You can't just make promises without telling me how you're going to follow up on them."

355.speaker: Narrator
355.text: She paused for a moment, as if deliberating.

356.speaker: Alma Saltana
356.text: "I will tell you that Lespia has contacted us regarding a very similar arrangement."

357.speaker: Alma Saltana
357.text: "But if you're sure Rizia will be able to deliver a steady supply of energy to Morella, we would be happy to go with you instead."

358.speaker: Player_Romus
358.text: "Absolutely. I am a king who delivers on his promises."

360.speaker: Alma Saltana
360.text: "Then you obviously should not be making this demand."

363.speaker: Alma Saltana
363.text: "I'll tell you right away that I do not want to have any contact with Duke Reinhart."

364.speaker: Player_Romus
364.text: "Well, Rizia has a large amount of energy to sell."

365.speaker: Alma Saltana
365.text: "I presume you're referring to the gas field off the Palesian coast?"

366.speaker: Player_Romus
366.text: "He's not so bad. You'd like him if you got to know him."

368.speaker: Player_Romus
368.text: "It would send a strong signal to the superpowers. South Merkopa can rely on itself."

369.speaker: Player_Romus
369.text: "You don't believe that we can fulfil our end of it?"

370.speaker: Alma Saltana
370.text: "Would this energy come from the gas field off the Palesian coast?"

371.speaker: Alma Saltana
371.text: "It would also send a signal to your coalition of monarchies. GRACE, was it?"

374.speaker: Alma Saltana
374.text: "Would this energy come from the gas field off the Palesian coast? I'll tell you right away that I do not want to have any contact with Duke Reinhart."

378.speaker: Player_Romus
378.text: "Pales may own the field, but Rizia has the full rights to it. We can decide what is done with it."

379.speaker: Player_Romus
379.text: "Leave the dealings with the Duke to us. Rizia will handle everything."

383.speaker: Player_Romus
383.text: "We also have access to oil from Wehlen. We can build a pipeline straight to Cavette."

384.speaker: Player_Romus
384.text: "Not necessarily. We have other energy sources."

386.speaker: Alma Saltana
386.text: "I will tolerate Pales. But I will not 'like' the ruler whose family occupied my country for over a century."

389.speaker: Alma Saltana
389.text: "If you can get their Supreme Wiseman to agree to that, we would be interested."

391.speaker: Alma Saltana
391.text: "I'm wary of entering into an energy arrangement with the man whose family occupied my country for over a century. Even an indirect one."

392.speaker: Alma Saltana
392.text: "But we don't have many alternatives at the moment. I will consider it."

393.speaker: Alma Saltana
393.text: "I'm wary of entering into an energy arrangement with the man whose family occupied my country for over a century. Even an indirect one."

394.speaker: Alma Saltana
394.text: "I would rather not harm our upcoming round of negotiations with Lespia."

395.speaker: Alma Saltana
395.text: "On the other hand, I would certainly rather that field ended up in Rizian than Palesian hands."

397.speaker: Alma Saltana
397.text: "I'll remind you that I do have some leverage, in the form of an energy proposal from Lespia."

401.speaker: Alma Saltana
401.text: "In fact... Prime Minister Alvarez has requested to buy Rizia's share of the MITZ in addition to Lespia's own."

402.speaker: Alma Saltana
402.text: "We were planning on meeting a limited number of your demands in addition to offering you a 20 percent share in the new ITZ."

403.speaker: Alma Saltana
403.text: "But if you forgo that share entirely, as Valgsland has done, we'll gladly make it worth your while."

404.speaker: Player_Romus
404.text: "What if I want to buy Lespia's share along with Rizia's?"

405.speaker: Alma Saltana
405.text: "Giving your kingdom a 40 percent stake in the restructured MITZ?"

406.speaker: Alma Saltana
406.text: "In that case, {RiziaDLCText.SaltanaToPlayer}, Morella would be the country making the demands."

407.speaker: Player_Romus
407.text: "Is that what you're offering Lespia as well?"

408.speaker: Player_Romus
408.text: "Damn. I was about to ask whether Rizia could buy Lespia's share."

409.speaker: Player_Romus
409.text: "That greedy bastard. I hope you turned him down."

410.speaker: Player_Romus
410.text: "And what would Rizia have to do to prevent that from happening?"

411.speaker: Player_Romus
411.text: "You'd accept energy from Lespia *and* grant them a 40 percent stake in the MITZ? Valgsland would hate that."

412.speaker: Player_Romus
412.text: "The same way you made it worth Valgsland's while?"

413.speaker: Alma Saltana
413.text: "We're not expecting Lespia's approval on the final proposal. So except for the share offer, we don't feel compelled to be as generous."

414.speaker: Alma Saltana
414.text: "And we do want to make up for your kingdom's loss of revenue. We know how important gold has been to Rizia in the past."

415.speaker: Player_Romus
415.text: "I've heard great things about Morellan-built aircraft. I would like some for the Rizian air force."

416.speaker: Alma Saltana
416.text: "That can be arranged. Not for free, but we'll give you a good price on our best stock."

417.speaker: Alma Saltana
417.text: "Is there a specific reason why you're interested in strengthening your air force right now?"

418.speaker: Player_Romus
418.text: "We have ATO member states to our north and south. We must be able to defend ourselves from their encroaching influence."

422.speaker: Player_Romus
422.text: "I am worried about escalation with Pales. We must be prepared in case of conflict."

423.speaker: Player_Romus
423.text: "We need a strong military if our kingdom is to assert our relevance in the 20th century."

426.speaker: Narrator
426.text: She looked satisfied with my answer.

427.speaker: Alma Saltana
427.text: "My government has had the same concerns. Particularly regarding our Qinali neighbors."

428.speaker: Alma Saltana
428.text: "Our own conflict with Pales is long over. I was hoping it would stay that way."

429.speaker: Alma Saltana
429.text: "It is Rizia's system of government that needs to be brought into the modern age, not its artillery."

431.speaker: Alma Saltana
431.text: "We are direct neighbors. If you have big plans involving your military, I'd appreciate knowing about them."

434.speaker: Alma Saltana
434.text: "We can't top the size or firepower of their military. But we can show the West we will not be easily intimidated."

438.speaker: Alma Saltana
438.text: "But if the situation did escalate, we would be obliged to support you."

442.speaker: Alma Saltana
442.text: "We can't promise any direct support in case of escalation. I hope our aircraft suffices."

443.speaker: Alma Saltana
443.text: "But I understand the need to keep pace. We've stepped up our own military efforts as Qinal and Derdia have increased theirs."

447.speaker: Alma Saltana
447.text: "Exercise modesty in your negotiations. That's all."

448.speaker: Alma Saltana
448.text: "I don't want Lespia to come away with a 40 percent stake any more than you do."

449.speaker: Alma Saltana
449.text: "Where we get our energy from is up to us, not Chancellor Hegel."

450.speaker: Alma Saltana
450.text: "And I don't think either of us wants Lespia to come away with a 40 percent stake. But if I can't secure Rizia's cooperation, I'll have to look elsewhere."

451.speaker: Alma Saltana
451.text: "Believe it or not, Valgsland refused to accept anything other than standard compensation for its assets."

455.speaker: Alma Saltana
455.text: "I'm sure the Chancellor's requests will come later, though."

456.speaker: Alma Saltana
456.text: "You heard the Chancellor during the meeting. His republic is still atoning for the Valgos Empire's past wrongs."

457.speaker: Alma Saltana
457.text: "With that said, should it prove difficult to secure your kingdom's cooperation, we'll be forced to turn to them."

458.speaker: Alma Saltana
458.text: "But if Morella can't secure Rizia's cooperation, we'll have no choice but to turn elsewhere."

459.speaker: Narrator
459.text: The waiter came by and took away our empty teacups. Saltana waited until he was gone, then looked at me.

460.speaker: Narrator
460.text: The waiter came by and took away our empty teacups. Saltana waited until he was gone, then looked at me.

461.speaker: Alma Saltana
461.text: "Tell me. Does Rizia wish to purchase a share in the nationalized MITZ or not?"

462.speaker: Player_Romus
462.text: "No, my kingdom will not accept a share. It's more important to have Morella's support in all the matters I mentioned earlier."

463.speaker: Player_Romus
463.text: "Yes. We will accept your offer of a 20 percent share in the restructured Trade Zone."

464.speaker: Player_Romus
464.text: "First, let's talk about what Rizia would have to do to buy Lespia's share."

467.speaker: Alma Saltana
467.text: "First of all, we are still interested in an energy deal with Rizia, but one where we have more control over the terms and prices."

471.speaker: Alma Saltana
471.text: "We would also ask that you contribute a small sum of money towards the rehabilitation of the Arufelde watershed."

472.speaker: Alma Saltana
472.text: "Barring that, we would ask that you contribute money towards the rehabilitation of the Arufelde watershed."

474.speaker: Alma Saltana
474.text: "We require assistance in dealing with the Derdians attempting to infiltrate our borders."

475.speaker: Player_Romus
475.text: "Gladly. Those radical Golcondists are a threat to all of us."

476.speaker: Player_Romus
476.text: "Infiltrate? All they're trying to do is reach the same sanctuaries where their ancestors prayed."

482.speaker: Alma Saltana
482.text: "I'm grateful for your border ban in Rizia, by the way. We're seeing significantly fewer insurgents trying to reach your country through ours."

483.speaker: Alma Saltana
483.text: "*All* of them? We'll have to see about that."

484.speaker: Player_Romus
484.text: "No share. And we're not going to make any demands of you, either. Nationalization is its own reward."

486.speaker: Alma Saltana
486.text: "Well, you're welcome to change your mind before the proposal is finalized."

487.speaker: Alma Saltana
487.text: "Most of the Derdians entering Morella are trying to migrate to Rizia. So this is your problem as much as it is ours."

489.speaker: Alma Saltana
489.text: "Don't fall for that argument. I'm generally a tolerant person, but the Derdians spread chaos wherever they go."

490.speaker: Alma Saltana
490.text: "Azmal refuses to talk to me. Can you guess why?"

491.speaker: Player_Romus
491.text: "I can already tell you I am not interested in angering the Supreme Wiseman."

495.speaker: Alma Saltana
495.text: "It's a little late for that. He's already mad as hell over your border ban."

496.speaker: Alma Saltana
496.text: "You wouldn't have to make him angry."

498.speaker: Player_Romus
498.text: "Because you have the temperament of a petulant child."

500.speaker: Player_Romus
500.text: "Because of the lingering animosity between your countries."

501.speaker: Alma Saltana
501.text: "An agnostic Zaranist, actually. But no, the Supreme Wiseman refuses to negotiate with female leaders."

502.speaker: Alma Saltana
502.text: "Exactly. The Supreme Wiseman refuses to negotiate with female leaders."

503.speaker: Alma Saltana
503.text: "You'd think that would be a factor. But no, the Supreme Wiseman simply refuses to negotiate with female leaders."

504.speaker: Narrator
504.text: She sat back and glared at me.

505.speaker: Alma Saltana
505.text: "Do you insult your councilors like this, too?"

509.speaker: Alma Saltana
509.text: "But no. The Supreme Wiseman refuses to negotiate with female leaders."

510.speaker: Alma Saltana
510.text: "But I have a hunch he will respect a king and fellow Wruhecist."

514.speaker: Alma Saltana
514.text: "But I have a hunch he will respect a king and fellow Wruhecist. Your border ban notwithstanding."

515.speaker: Player_Romus
515.text: "You're right. This is best settled between us men."

519.speaker: Player_Romus
519.text: "We both walk in the light of the six stars. Surely we'll be able to find common ground."

520.speaker: Player_Romus
520.text: "This is not my kingdom's conflict. I'd rather not get involved in it."

521.speaker: Player_Romus
521.text: "I can try my best. But I doubt I'd be able to get through to him."

527.speaker: Alma Saltana
527.text: "Your help would be appreciated, but if you're willing to fulfill the other two conditions I mentioned, I would let this one go."

528.speaker: Alma Saltana
528.text: "Your help would be appreciated, but if you're willing to fulfill even one of the other two conditions I mentioned, I would let this one go."

529.speaker: Alma Saltana
529.text: "Does that mean you're still interested in purchasing Lespia's share?"

531.speaker: Player_Romus
531.text: "You drive a hard bargain. But yes, I still want Rizia to have Lespia's share."

532.speaker: Player_Romus
532.text: "No, I'd rather go back to making the demands. I'll stick with a 20 percent share for Rizia."

533.speaker: Player_Romus
533.text: "No. Actually, I don't want a share in the new Trade Zone at all."

534.speaker: Alma Saltana
534.text: "Thank you. We'll make sure you are well compensated for your loss of income."

535.speaker: Narrator
535.text: She brushed some biscuit crumbs off the tablecloth.

536.speaker: Alma Saltana
536.text: "The details will have to be worked out with the help of my ministers and your councilors. This is too formal an arrangement to be signed over tea, I'm afraid."

538.speaker: Alma Saltana
538.text: "You're as cutthroat as the Lespians, in your own way. I can't decide whether I admire it or not."

544.speaker: Alma Saltana
544.text: "I admit our biscuits are an acquired taste. Like our politics."

548.speaker: Narrator
548.text: She nibbled on the corner of her own biscuit, then took a slow, deliberate sip of tea.

549.speaker: Alma Saltana
549.text: "You should know that while the MITZ as a whole will not be nationalized, Morella and Valgsland have come to an agreement on our own."

550.speaker: Alma Saltana
550.text: "Chancellor Hegel is turning over his country's stake in the Trade Zone to Morella, in exchange for standard compensation and a continued presence on the board."

551.speaker: Player_Romus
551.text: "You're fooling yourself if you think Rizia will do the same."

552.speaker: Player_Romus
552.text: "Just like with Valgsland's former colonies. Faking 'generosity' so he can place you in his debt."

556.speaker: Player_Romus
556.text: "That's audacious. Neither Rizia nor Lespia have approved such a sale."

557.speaker: Player_Romus
557.text: "That's only fair. He did say he wanted to atone for the Valgos Empire's misdeeds."

558.speaker: Alma Saltana
558.text: "I don't expect that at all. But I do expect change."

559.speaker: Alma Saltana
559.text: "Typical anti-Malenyevism. You'd never agree to lose money without an ulterior motive, so you accuse everyone else of having one too."

560.speaker: Alma Saltana
560.text: "What Valgsland chooses to do with its share is not Rizia's business."

561.speaker: Alma Saltana
561.text: "It is a step in the right direction."

565.speaker: Alma Saltana
565.text: "That means regulations similar to the ones you already passed in Rizia, applied to every company that is active in the Trade Zone."

566.speaker: Alma Saltana
566.text: "That means regulations similar to the ones you already passed in Rizia -- but applicable to mining corporations."

570.speaker: Alma Saltana
570.text: "That means regulations guaranteeing mine workers  a living wage, limiting overtime and promoting safety. Applicable to every stakeholder in the MITZ."

571.speaker: Player_Romus
571.text: "That's only fair. A company's standards should be the same, no matter the country in which it's operating."

572.speaker: Player_Romus
572.text: "That is a fair request. I will consider supporting it."

573.speaker: Player_Romus
573.text: "That'll be a problem. I passed those regulations in Rizia because I knew our MITZ profits could make up for the loss of income."

574.speaker: Player_Romus
574.text: "I already regret passing those regulations. The financial burden was more crushing than I expected."

575.speaker: Player_Romus
575.text: "Have you ever worked in a mine in your life? How can you claim to speak for miners?"

578.speaker: Alma Saltana
578.text: "We already have a draft co-authored by a panel of Morellans with current or former experience working in the Trade Zone."

580.speaker: Player_Romus
580.text: "I sympathize with the workers' plight. But my parliament believes such regulations are an unfair financial burden to corporations."

581.speaker: Alma Saltana
581.text: "Your parliament. You'll forgive me if I don't take that seriously."

582.speaker: Alma Saltana
582.text: "I hope you'll do more than consider it."

583.speaker: Player_Romus
583.text: "It's the voice of my people. I have to do what they say."

584.speaker: Alma Saltana
584.text: "I'm sorry. Did the jackal who runs your gold corporation have to sell one of his five houses?"

585.speaker: Alma Saltana
585.text: "So you were literally banking on the exploitation of Morellans? Sorry if I don't sympathize."

587.speaker: Player_Romus
587.text: "The majority speaker is well connected to Rizia's businesses. She knows more than anyone about the potential impacts of these laws."

588.speaker: Player_Romus
588.text: "Normally, they are more of a hindrance than a help. But in this case, I agree with them."

589.speaker: Alma Saltana
589.text: "Curious that the wishes of 'your people' and those of the monarchy so often align."

590.speaker: Alma Saltana
590.text: "I'm sure she knows all about their impacts on corporations. But on people?"

591.speaker: Alma Saltana
591.text: "So you admit your legislative body is a 'hindrance'."

592.speaker: Alma Saltana
592.text: "Regardless of your... parliament's wishes, this is what I want for the gold mines on my land."

593.speaker: Player_Romus
593.text: "You will not insult my country's most prominent businessman."

594.speaker: Player_Romus
594.text: "I have little sympathy for the CEO of Rizian Royal Gold. But in this case, he was right."

595.speaker: Player_Romus
595.text: "We both know it's more complicated than that. A sizeable portion of Rizia's economy relies on RRG."

596.speaker: Alma Saltana
596.text: "I am not beholden to Rizian Royal Gold in any way. I stand by what I said."

597.speaker: Alma Saltana
597.text: "The mortality risk of miners working in the Trade Zone is twice as high as that of regular Morellans. The boost to our countries' economies is not worth human lives."

598.speaker: Player_Romus
598.text: "To be fair, every job comes with risks. I could be beheaded at any time."

599.speaker: Player_Romus
599.text: "Still, we'd be losing quite a bit of money. It'll be hard to justify that to my government."

600.speaker: Alma Saltana
600.text: "Harder to justify than a total stalemate among MITZ stakeholders?"

601.speaker: Player_Romus
601.text: "You're absolutely right. People should always come before profits."

602.speaker: Alma Saltana
602.text: "The mortality risk of miners working in the Trade Zone is twice as high as that of regular Morellans. The boost to our countries' economies is not worth human lives."

603.speaker: Player_Romus
603.text: "Think of all the human lives that have improved thanks to that gold. It's not that bad of a trade-off, really."

605.speaker: Alma Saltana
605.text: "A glib way of putting it. But yes."

606.speaker: Alma Saltana
606.text: "That kind of tyrant's logic is what makes kingdoms fall."

608.speaker: Alma Saltana
608.text: "What about the people whose lives improved because of the laws you passed? Do they count for nothing?"

609.speaker: Alma Saltana
609.text: "It makes no sense that people on one side of our border should suffer so the other side can live in blind luxury."

612.speaker: Alma Saltana
612.text: "I... You know very well what I meant."

614.speaker: Alma Saltana
614.text: "I'm assuming by your lack of a response that I have made myself clear."

615.speaker: Player_Romus
615.text: "Would you also approve the reallocation of Lespia's ITZ share to Rizia?"

617.speaker: Alma Saltana
617.text: "In any event, you're making a very bold request."

618.speaker: Alma Saltana
618.text: "Raising Rizia's stake in the MITZ to 50 percent would put you precipitously close to a takeover."

619.speaker: Player_Romus
619.text: "What if we shrank Rizia's share in the new agreement? Morella would have majority control of the MITZ, and you could implement as much oversight as you wanted."

621.speaker: Alma Saltana
621.text: "Of course that would be wonderful. But what would Rizia be getting out of it?"

622.speaker: Player_Romus
622.text: "Actually, let's talk about everyone's shares staying the same. What would it take for Morella to vote to keep the MITZ the way it is?"

623.speaker: Player_Romus
623.text: "But we'd be a more trustworthy partner than Lespia."

628.speaker: Player_Romus
628.text: "We wouldn't try anything. Rizia is completely on board with your vision for the future of the MITZ."

629.speaker: Player_Romus
629.text: "We are prepared to sweeten the deal."

630.speaker: Player_Romus
630.text: "Why doesn't Morella take Lespia's share as well? We don't need their final approval as long as Valgsland is still on board."

631.speaker: Alma Saltana
631.text: "I'm surprised you would suggest that. You and the Prime Minister seemed to be on the same page during the board meeting."

636.speaker: Alma Saltana
636.text: "No offense, but you had better be."

637.speaker: Narrator
637.text: She looked me in the eye.

641.speaker: Alma Saltana
641.text: "As it happens, Lespia recently contacted us with an attractive energy proposition. To gain the upper hand in our upcoming negotiations, I suspect."

642.speaker: Alma Saltana
642.text: "Shutting them out of the MITZ completely would therefore require a substantial commitment from you."

643.speaker: Player_Romus
643.text: "We want to make a good faith effort to build closer bonds with our neighbors. This is part of it."

644.speaker: Player_Romus
644.text: "It would put you in our debt. There are things Rizia needs more than gold."

645.speaker: Player_Romus
645.text: "Watching as Lespia is forced to comply with your rules would be enough of a reward for me."

646.speaker: Alma Saltana
646.text: "I believe you. But you're asking for too much."

647.speaker: Alma Saltana
647.text: "Even if we'd gone through with nationalization, I never would have cut Lespia out of the MITZ completely. Their contributions to it have been too great."

649.speaker: Player_Romus
649.text: "We're prepared to top whatever Mr. Alvarez is offering. Just tell me what you want."

650.speaker: Player_Romus
650.text: "A substantial commitment? Forget I asked, then."

651.speaker: Player_Romus
651.text: "An energy deal with Lespia? Valgsland wouldn't like that at all."

652.speaker: Alma Saltana
652.text: "Agreeing to transfer their share to Rizia would therefore require a substantial commitment from you."

653.speaker: Player_Romus
653.text: "Wouldn't watching Mr. Alvarez's face as he realizes he's walking away with nothing be its own reward?"

655.speaker: Alma Saltana
655.text: "We are on the verge of exhausting our own oil reserves. We cannot be picky."

656.speaker: Alma Saltana
656.text: "I thought as much. It'll be easier to go with another plan."

657.speaker: Alma Saltana
657.text: "Here's what it would take to turn down Lespia's offer and allow Rizia to purchase their share."

659.speaker: Player_Romus
659.text: "He's an untrustworthy drunk. The MITZ is better off without him."

660.speaker: Player_Romus
660.text: "We were. But my mind has changed since then."

661.speaker: Alma Saltana
661.text: "But if you'd rather accept compensation, our offers still stand."

662.speaker: Player_Romus
662.text: "Perhaps so, but he was always going to betray me. I'm just getting ahead of him."

663.speaker: Alma Saltana
663.text: "I can't say I dislike the idea."

675.speaker: Alma Saltana
675.text: "I'm surprised you would suggest that. You and the Prime Minister seemed to be on the same page during the board meeting."

676.speaker: Player_Romus
676.text: "He's an untrustworthy drunk. The MITZ is better off without him."

677.speaker: Player_Romus
677.text: "We were. But my mind has changed since then."

678.speaker: Player_Romus
678.text: "Perhaps so, but he was always going to betray me. I'm just getting ahead of him."

682.speaker: Alma Saltana
682.text: "That would require a much more substantial commitment from Rizia than what we discussed earlier."

684.speaker: Alma Saltana
684.text: "We would like to discuss a favorable energy supplier arrangement with Rizian Oil and Gas. With all necessary infrastructure handled and paid for by your government."

685.speaker: Alma Saltana
685.text: "We'd require your assistance in dealing with the Derdians attempting to infiltrate our borders."

686.speaker: Player_Romus
686.text: "Gladly. Those radical Golcondists are a threat to all of us."

687.speaker: Player_Romus
687.text: "Infiltrate? All they're trying to do is reach the same sanctuaries where their ancestors prayed."

693.speaker: Alma Saltana
693.text: "I'm grateful for your border ban in Rizia, by the way. We're seeing significantly fewer insurgents trying to reach your country through ours."

694.speaker: Alma Saltana
694.text: "Most of the Derdians entering Morella are trying to migrate to Rizia. So this is your problem as much as it is ours."

696.speaker: Alma Saltana
696.text: "Don't fall for that argument. I'm generally a tolerant person, but the Derdians spread chaos wherever they go."

697.speaker: Alma Saltana
697.text: "Azmal refuses to talk to me. Can you guess why?"

698.speaker: Player_Romus
698.text: "I can already tell you I am not interested in angering the Supreme Wiseman."

702.speaker: Alma Saltana
702.text: "It's a little late for that. He's already mad as hell over your border ban."

703.speaker: Alma Saltana
703.text: "You wouldn't have to make him angry."

705.speaker: Player_Romus
705.text: "Because you have the manners of a petulant child."

707.speaker: Player_Romus
707.text: "Because of the lingering animosity between your countries."

708.speaker: Alma Saltana
708.text: "An agnostic Zaranist, actually. But no, the Supreme Wiseman refuses to negotiate with female leaders."

709.speaker: Alma Saltana
709.text: "Exactly. The Supreme Wiseman refuses to negotiate with female leaders."

710.speaker: Alma Saltana
710.text: "You'd think that would be a factor. But no, the Supreme Wiseman simply refuses to negotiate with female leaders."

711.speaker: Narrator
711.text: She sat back and glared at me.

712.speaker: Alma Saltana
712.text: "Do you insult your councilors like that, too?"

716.speaker: Alma Saltana
716.text: "But no. The Supreme Wiseman refuses to negotiate with female leaders."

720.speaker: Player_Romus
720.text: "You're right. This is best settled between us men."

721.speaker: Player_Romus
721.text: "We both walk in the light of the six stars. Surely we'll be able to find common ground."

725.speaker: Player_Romus
725.text: "This is not my kingdom's conflict. I'd rather not get involved in it."

727.speaker: Alma Saltana
727.text: "But I have a hunch he will respect a king and fellow Wruhecist."

728.speaker: Alma Saltana
728.text: "Your own treatment of Golcondists cannot have escaped Derdia's attention. The conflict will come to Rizia sooner or later."

729.speaker: Alma Saltana
729.text: "For both of our countries' sake, I hope you do."

730.speaker: Alma Saltana
730.text: "But I have a hunch he will respect a king and fellow Wruhecist. Your border ban notwithstanding."

731.speaker: Player_Romus
731.text: "I can try my best. But I doubt I'd be able to get through to him."

733.speaker: Player_Romus
733.text: "We're already building a gas pipeline from Pales to Rizia. It should be no problem to extend it to Morella."

737.speaker: Player_Romus
737.text: "Perfect. We'll be looking for new customers once the Alliance of Nation grants us the rights to our new gas field."

741.speaker: Player_Romus
741.text: "That might prove difficult. We have pre-existing energy arrangements with other countries."

744.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
744.conditionsRaw: (Variable["RiziaDLC.Situation_Diplomacy_Rumburg_HighEnergyExport"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.Situation_Diplomacy_Rumburg_AverageEnergyExport"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.Situation_Diplomacy_Wehlen_ExportGas"] == true) == false

745.speaker: Player_Romus
745.text: "I'd love to be able to promise you a steady supply of energy. But I am not sure I can."

746.speaker: Player_Romus
746.text: "Certainly, Madam Prime Minister. Our energy stores are as robust as ever."

748.speaker: Alma Saltana
748.text: "If you're not willing to make this deal, you'll have to be content with a smaller share."

755.speaker: Player_Romus
755.text: "Leave the dealings with the Duke to us. Rizia will handle everything."

756.speaker: Player_Romus
756.text: "Past is past, Ms. Saltana. The current Duke respects Morella's sovereignty."

757.speaker: Player_Romus
757.text: "Pales may own the field, but Rizia has the full rights to it. We can decide what is done with it."

758.speaker: Alma Saltana
758.text: "I'm still wary of getting Morella re-involved with Pales, even indirectly. But a pipeline does seem convenient."

759.speaker: Alma Saltana
759.text: "I will tell you right away that I don't want anything to do with Reinhart."

766.speaker: Alma Saltana
766.text: "In fact, I don't think I can agree on that unless you agree to all of the demands I mentioned earlier."

770.speaker: Alma Saltana
770.text: "There would still be some room for negotiation. But the pollution reparations, the energy deal and the Derdian border assistance would all be on the table."
770.conditionsRaw: (Variable["RiziaDLC.Diplomacy_Lespia_GasField_25PercentDeal"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.Diplomacy_Pales_GasField_Cede"] == true) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Diplomacy_Lespia_GasField_25PercentDeal"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.Diplomacy_Pales_GasField_Cede"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Diplomacy_Morella_NegotiatingPower"] < 0) == false)

772.speaker: Alma Saltana
772.text: "But I might agree to take their share, in exchange for at least a few of the demands I mentioned earlier."

773.speaker: Alma Saltana
773.text: "Why are you suggesting this? What would be in it for Rizia?"

774.speaker: Player_Romus
774.text: "Getting Western influence out of the MITZ is a win for all of us."

775.speaker: Player_Romus
775.text: "Don't worry about what would be in it for us. You deserve this."

776.speaker: Player_Romus
776.text: "The MITZ would be managed by two neighboring countries. You must see the benefit in that."

777.speaker: Alma Saltana
777.text: "Is that you talking? Or Chancellor Hegel?"

778.speaker: Alma Saltana
778.text: "I can't just ignore the offer that Lespia made us."

782.speaker: Alma Saltana
782.text: "As I said, I am hesitant to completely shut Lespia out of the mining center that they helped build."

783.speaker: Alma Saltana
783.text: "The problem is that Prime Minister Alvarez recently contacted us with an attractive energy proposition. To gain the upper hand in our upcoming negotiations, I suspect."

784.speaker: Alma Saltana
784.text: "As we are on the verge of exhausting our own oil reserves, I'm obliged to hear him out."

786.speaker: Player_Romus
786.text: "We're prepared to top whatever Mr. Alvarez is offering."

787.speaker: Player_Romus
787.text: "An energy deal with Lespia? Valgsland wouldn't like that at all."

788.speaker: Alma Saltana
788.text: "Until Valgsland can offer us energy, they have no say in where we get ours."

789.speaker: Alma Saltana
789.text: "With that said, I'd be willing to turn Alvarez down and agree to what you're suggesting, in exchange for a minor commitment or two from Rizia."

790.speaker: Alma Saltana
790.text: "You wouldn't have to top it. But we would ask for a commitment."

793.speaker: Alma Saltana
793.text: "Why are you even suggesting this? What would be in it for Rizia?"

794.speaker: Player_Romus
794.text: "Getting Western influence out of the MITZ is a win for all of us."

795.speaker: Player_Romus
795.text: "Don't worry about what would be in it for us. You deserve this."

796.speaker: Player_Romus
796.text: "The MITZ would be managed by two neighboring countries. You must see the benefit in that."

797.speaker: Alma Saltana
797.text: "And they accuse *me* of parroting Chancellor Hegel?"

798.speaker: Alma Saltana
798.text: "I do. But even if the nationalization vote had gone through, my plan was never to leave Lespia with nothing."

799.speaker: Alma Saltana
799.text: "Even if the nationalization vote had gone through, my plan was never to leave Lespia with nothing."

800.speaker: Alma Saltana
800.text: "With that said, I'd be willing agree to what you're suggesting, in exchange for a minor commitment from Rizia."

803.speaker: Alma Saltana
803.text: "I thought as much. It'll be easier to go with another plan."

805.speaker: Alma Saltana
805.text: "We've had our experts draw up an initial plan. It includes river cleaning initiatives, water purification systems for affected communities and increased penalties for environmental violations committed by mining companies."

806.speaker: Player_Romus
806.text: "I'm willing to pay whatever it takes to clean up the mess our companies made."

807.speaker: Alma Saltana
807.text: "I won't lie. It will be costly."

808.speaker: Player_Romus
808.text: "I made that donation because I was feeling philanthropic. It wasn't meant as reparations."

812.speaker: Alma Saltana
812.text: "However, your previous donation should entitle you to pay less."

813.speaker: Alma Saltana
813.text: "But I hope you'll agree that this is a necessary step towards rebuilding the trust between ITZ partners."

814.speaker: Player_Romus
814.text: "Don't forget that Morella was also involved in the river pollution."

815.speaker: Player_Romus
815.text: "Rizia never broke any laws. We shouldn't have to pay at all."

816.speaker: Alma Saltana
816.text: "You didn't break the laws because they didn't exist. An omission that we are only now rectifying."

817.speaker: Alma Saltana
817.text: "The intent doesn't matter, {RiziaDLCText.SaltanaToPlayer}. Money is money."

818.speaker: Alma Saltana
818.text: "I am not excluding Morella from this responsibility. But we should not bear the burden alone."

830.speaker: Alma Saltana
830.text: "We would also ask for the following."

831.speaker: Alma Saltana
831.text: "First, a financial contribution towards the rehabilitation of the Arufelde river watershed."

832.speaker: Alma Saltana
832.text: "We would also ask for at least two of the following."
832.conditionsRaw: (Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn05_MorellaITZ_Shares_RiziaBuysLespia_InProgress"] == true) and ((Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn05_MorellaITZ_Shares_RiziaBuysLespia_InProgress"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Diplomacy_Morella_NegotiatingPower"] < 0) == false) and (Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn05_MorellaITZ_Shares_MorellaBuysLespia_InProgress"] == true) and (Variable["RiziaDLC.Diplomacy_Morella_NegotiatingPower"] < 0)

833.speaker: Alma Saltana
833.text: "We would also ask for at least one of the following."
833.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn05_MorellaITZ_Shares_RiziaBuysLespia_InProgress"] == true) == false) and (Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn05_MorellaITZ_Shares_MorellaBuysLespia_InProgress"] == true) and ((Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn05_MorellaITZ_Shares_MorellaBuysLespia_InProgress"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Diplomacy_Morella_NegotiatingPower"] < 0) == false) and (Variable["RiziaDLC.Diplomacy_Morella_NegotiatingPower"] < 0)

841.speaker: Alma Saltana
841.text: "If that is absolutely not an option for Rizia, we would ask for one of the following."
841.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn05_MorellaITZ_Shares_RiziaBuysLespia_InProgress"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn05_MorellaITZ_Shares_MorellaBuysLespia_InProgress"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Diplomacy_Morella_NegotiatingPower"] < 0) == false)

846.speaker: Player_Romus
846.text: "While we're talking about the reallocation of shares... I have a proposal for you."

847.speaker: Player_Romus
847.text: "So Morella will have a 50 percent share in the MITZ. What else could you want?"

852.speaker: Alma Saltana
852.text: "If Morella is to approve any new agreement for the Meftiem ITZ, it should include better worker protections at the very minimum."

857.speaker: Alma Saltana
857.text: "If that's what you believe, I'm confused you didn't just vote for nationalization."

858.speaker: Alma Saltana
858.text: "If you wanted to make a truly good-faith effort, you would've supported my nationalization plan. But I appreciate the gesture."

859.speaker: Alma Saltana
859.text: "I see. And here I thought you were being altruistic."

860.speaker: Alma Saltana
860.text: "Agreeing on a smaller share would indeed entitle you to ask favors of us."

861.speaker: Alma Saltana
861.text: "We'd be prepared to grant you favors in return. But not too many."

862.speaker: Player_Romus
862.text: "We want an energy deal. But one where we control the terms and prices."

863.speaker: Player_Romus
863.text: "We'd ask for Morella's assistance in extricating the territory of Zille from Wehzek hands."

864.speaker: Player_Romus
864.text: "We want a deal on Morellan airplanes. Rizia needs a stronger air force."

865.speaker: Player_Romus
865.text: "We wouldn't ask for much. Only your support in the gas field arbitration proceedings with Pales."

869.speaker: Player_Romus
869.text: "No favors. This is the least we can do."

872.speaker: Alma Saltana
872.text: "I'm still confused. But I appreciate the offer."

882.speaker: Alma Saltana
882.text: "On Rizia's side, we would only want you to agree to new mining regulations. Or at the very least, one of the other demands I mentioned."
882.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn05_MorellaITZNonNationalization_DemandsShared"] == false) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Diplomacy_Lespia_GasField_25PercentDeal"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.Diplomacy_Pales_GasField_Cede"] == true) == false)

886.speaker: Alma Saltana
886.text: "We would want you to agree to new mining regulations, in addition to at least one of the other demands I mentioned."
886.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn05_MorellaITZNonNationalization_DemandsShared"] == false) == false) and (Variable["RiziaDLC.Diplomacy_Lespia_GasField_25PercentDeal"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.Diplomacy_Pales_GasField_Cede"] == true)

887.speaker: Player_Romus
887.text: "That's cheeky. All it would take is a stalemate between our four countries to maintain the status quo anyway."

888.speaker: Alma Saltana
888.text: "But would the status quo be maintained within the Rizian populace?"

889.speaker: Player_Romus
889.text: "That's reasonable, but do you really think Lespia will agree?"

890.speaker: Alma Saltana
890.text: "Morella's negotiations with Lespia are between myself and the Prime Minister."

891.speaker: Player_Romus
891.text: "You drive a hard bargain, Ms. Saltana."

892.speaker: Alma Saltana
892.text: "I am only asking for what my predecessors should have demanded long ago."

898.speaker: Alma Saltana
898.text: "Golcondism is spreading, I fear. The conflict will come to Rizia sooner or later."

911.speaker: Alma Saltana
911.text: "Do we have an agreement? Or are there other options you'd like to discuss?"
911.conditionsRaw: (Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn05_MorellaITZ_Shares_MorellaBuysLespia_InProgress"] == true) and ((Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn05_MorellaITZ_Shares_MorellaBuysLespia_InProgress"] == true) == false) and (Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn05_MorellaITZ_Shares_RiziaBuysLespia_InProgress"] == true) and ((Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn05_MorellaITZ_Shares_RiziaBuysLespia_InProgress"] == true) == false)

913.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
913.conditionsRaw: Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn05_MorellaITZ_Shares_StatusQuo"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn05_MorellaITZ_Shares_RiziaShrinks"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn05_MorellaITZ_Shares_RiziaBuysLespia"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn05_MorellaITZ_Shares_MorellaBuysLespia"] == true

914.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
914.conditionsRaw: (Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn05_MorellaITZ_Shares_StatusQuo"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn05_MorellaITZ_Shares_RiziaShrinks"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn05_MorellaITZ_Shares_RiziaBuysLespia"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn05_MorellaITZ_Shares_MorellaBuysLespia"] == true) == false

915.speaker: Player_Romus
915.text: "We've discussed this enough. Here's what I propose."
915.conditionsRaw: Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn05_MorellaITZ_Shares_StatusQuo"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn05_MorellaITZ_Shares_RiziaShrinks"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn05_MorellaITZ_Shares_RiziaBuysLespia"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn05_MorellaITZ_Shares_MorellaBuysLespia"] == true

918.speaker: Player_Romus
918.text: "I want Rizia and Lespia to keep our current shares. And I'm willing to meet your conditions to gain Morella's approval."

919.speaker: Player_Romus
919.text: "I want the new MITZ agreement to split the Trade Zone shares 50-50 between Rizia and Morella. Lespia will get nothing."

920.speaker: Player_Romus
920.text: "The new agreement should split the MITZ 75-25 between Morella and Rizia. We're kicking Lespia out of the Trade Zone."

921.speaker: Player_Romus
921.text: "Rizia will grant Morella part of our share, giving you majority control over the Trade Zone. But not without concessions from you."

922.speaker: Player_Romus
922.text: "There will be no new MITZ agreement. If we have to stay in a stalemate forever, so be it."

923.speaker: Narrator
923.text: She furiously pushed back her chair and stood up.

924.speaker: Alma Saltana
924.text: "I'm sorry to have wasted both of our time, then."

925.speaker: Alma Saltana
925.text: "But thank you for coming to the table. Literally and figuratively."

932.speaker: Alma Saltana
932.text: "That's the outcome I was hoping for."

934.speaker: Alma Saltana
934.text: "Lespia is closer to Rizia than to Morella. I hope you're prepared for the repercussions."

936.speaker: Alma Saltana
936.text: "Understood. I would call that a positive outcome."

937.speaker: Alma Saltana
937.text: "We will be in touch shortly regarding the exact details. I expect that Rizia will hold to whatever promises are made."

938.speaker: Alma Saltana
938.text: "We will be in touch shortly regarding the exact details. Needless to say, Morella will hold to whatever promises are made."

941.speaker: Player_Romus
941.text: "Halaita. If it is said, so it is, so it will be."

947.speaker: Player_Romus
947.text: "I look forward to working more closely together."

948.speaker: Alma Saltana
948.text: "You'll mostly be hearing from my cabinet. I prefer not to make unilateral decisions."

949.speaker: Narrator
949.text: She stood up and pushed her chair back.

950.speaker: Narrator
950.text: She stood up and pushed her chair back.

951.speaker: Player_Romus
951.text: "It wasn't a waste. Now I know my security forces should be on the lookout for Morellan revolutionaries."

952.speaker: Player_Romus
952.text: "It's not like that. I was also hoping we could find a solution that benefited all of us."

954.speaker: Player_Romus
954.text: "You should've known I'd never grant concessions to CSP cronies."

956.speaker: Alma Saltana
956.text: "Please feel free to take a biscuit for the trip back."

958.speaker: Alma Saltana
958.text: "What makes you think they'll be Morellan?"

960.speaker: Narrator
960.text: We left the teahouse and rejoined our guards outside.

962.speaker: Alma Saltana
962.text: "Feel free to take a biscuit for the trip home if you like."

963.speaker: Narrator
963.text: We left the teahouse and joined our guards outside.

970.speaker: Player_Romus
970.text: "This marks a new start for both of our countries."

971.speaker: Player_Romus
971.text: "I look forward to working more closely together."

972.speaker: Player_Romus
972.text: "I hope I can count on your support should the need arise."

975.speaker: Alma Saltana
975.text: "You'll mostly be hearing from my cabinet. I prefer not to make unilateral decisions."

976.speaker: Alma Saltana
976.text: "Let's see how this plan develops first."

977.speaker: Alma Saltana
977.text: "You're more used to the Rumburgian kind, I assume. But I think ours is better."

997.speaker: Narrator
997.text: Our plan was to discuss how to proceed with the nationalization of the Meftiem International Trade Zone.

998.speaker: Narrator
998.text: Her government had expressed its dissatisfaction with the results of the Meftiem International Trade Zone nationalization vote, and demanded a renegotiation of the agreement.

999.speaker: Narrator
999.text: My security detail and I exited our motorcade outside the gates of the People's Gardens, Cavette's largest park.

1000.speaker: Narrator
1000.text: Originally known as the Imperial Gardens, it had served as a private strolling ground for the Emperor of Moridia, then for the Reinhart family during the Valgish occupation.

1001.speaker: Narrator
1001.text: When Morella reconquered Cavette in 1923, the vast green area was opened to the public.

1002.speaker: Narrator
1002.text: Once immaculately landscaped with imported Valgish trees and flowers, the park was replanted with native Morellan flora and allowed to grow wild. Children played hide and seek in the tall grasses and raced each other up the conical hill in the center.

1003.speaker: Narrator
1003.text: Alma Saltana greeted me inside the gates, accompanied by only a small security retinue.

1008.speaker: Alma Saltana
1008.text: "We ended on a promising note the last time we saw each other. I hope we can continue that today."

1009.speaker: Player_Romus
1009.text: "Looks like this place could use a good groundskeeper."

1012.speaker: Alma Saltana
1012.text: "The Valgish conquerors thought they could bend our nature to their will. In the end, they failed."

1013.speaker: Alma Saltana
1013.text: "We can arrange a tour of one of our air force bases, if there's time after our talk."

1016.speaker: Player_Romus
1016.text: "You don't trust him either? That's interesting."

1017.speaker: Player_Romus
1017.text: "You can't be that naive. These 'reparations' are just another way for Valgsland to cling to its old territories."

1018.speaker: Player_Romus
1018.text: "Hegel does seem to take a genuine interest in Morella's welfare. I can understand the draw."

1019.speaker: Alma Saltana
1019.text: "To be clear, I trust him more than Patricio Alvarez. Or you, at this point."

1021.speaker: Alma Saltana
1021.text: "What would be the alternative? Allowing ex-colonies to slide into economic chaos? Letting the capitalist West take advantage of the power vacuum?"

1022.speaker: Alma Saltana
1022.text: "Yes, many of these former territories adopt socialist ideals. But they would take root even without Valgsland encouraging them to grow."

1023.speaker: Alma Saltana
1023.text: "Some of his ideas are too radical for my people to accept, I know. But we do see eye to eye in many cases."

1025.speaker: Player_Romus
1025.text: "Sure. It'll come in handy if there's a leak in my palace roof that needs plugging."

1026.speaker: Player_Romus
1026.text: "Thank you for the offer, but I'm very full."

1027.speaker: Player_Romus
1027.text: "Yes, please. I can't get enough of them."

1033.speaker: Player_Romus_Italic
1033.text: Give her the medallion from the MITZ.

1037.speaker: Alma Saltana
1037.text: "That's surprising. I hear they're an acquired taste to outsiders. But take as many as you like."

1039.speaker: Player_Romus
1039.text: "Never mind. Maybe I'll give it to you next time."

1041.speaker: Player_Romus
1041.text: "A little something to sweeten the deal."

1042.speaker: Player_Romus
1042.text: "Our contractors found this artifact in the MITZ. I believe it belongs to Morella."

1043.speaker: Narrator
1043.text: She stood up and pushed her chair back.

1045.speaker: Narrator
1045.text: With a somewhat confused look, she put the medallion in her briefcase.

1047.speaker: Alma Saltana
1047.text: "You are right. It does belong to us."

1052.speaker: Alma Saltana
1052.text: "That's very kind of you. I'll make sure your name is mentioned if we exhibit it in a museum."

1053.speaker: Narrator
1053.text: With a smile, she put the medallion in her briefcase.

1057.speaker: Player_Romus
1057.text: "The Lord is on the side of whoever wears this medallion. Please treasure it and keep it with you always."

1059.speaker: Player_Romus
1059.text: "Our greedy gold CEO wanted to keep this for himself. I told him it should stay in the country where it was found."

1063.speaker: Alma Saltana
1063.text: "I hope there's a next time, King Romus."

1065.speaker: Alma Saltana
1065.text: "For the gas you've bought from Pales?"

1066.speaker: Player_Romus
1066.text: "We ourselves are eager to find new energy partners as soon as possible."
1066.conditionsRaw: (Variable["RiziaDLC.Situation_Diplomacy_Rumburg_HighEnergyExport"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.Situation_Diplomacy_Rumburg_AverageEnergyExport"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.Situation_Diplomacy_Wehlen_ExportGas"] == true) == false

1074.speaker: Narrator
1074.text: I bit into mine. It was dry, crumbly and barely sweet -- perfect for washing down with a sip of tea.

1076.speaker: Narrator
1076.text: I bit into mine. It was dry, crumbly and barely sweet -- perfect for washing down with a sip of tea.

1085.speaker: Alma Saltana
1085.text: "Then you won't mind granting Morella a friendly discount."
